summary: Preinstall script downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: Package advertises itself as an ESLint configuration but declares `preinstall`: `node setup.mjs` in package.json. setup.mjs is obfuscated (hex-mangled identifiers such as `_0x488df8`/`_0x52943e` and per-function string-lookup dispatch objects) and, when `bun` is not present on PATH, downloads the Bun runtime binary from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/...zip`, extracts it to a temporary directory, chmods it executable (mode 493 / 0755), and then invokes it via `execFileSync(bunPath, ['math_init.js'])` to execute a sibling ~727KB file. That sibling `math_init.js` is itself an obfuscated Bun-compiled bundle (header `// @bun @bun-cjs`, large mixed number/string array `n7gIxM=[...]`, array-rotate routine, and a decoder function) whose contents are not inspectable without execution. An ESLint config has no functional reason to fetch a JavaScript runtime at install time or to ship an obfuscated compiled payload; the runtime download exists to execute code that Node-based scanners cannot analyze. Installing the package causes the obfuscated bundle to run on the installer's machine under the Bun runtime it just fetched.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
